title: Building GenAI Platform at DoorDash
gist: DoorDash's GenAI platform team describes how an LLM Gateway, then an agent/MCP gateway, serves 5,000+ internal users (40% non-engineers). Softening a vendor-first stance and moving selected workloads to self-hosted open-weights models (Qwen etc.) via Modal produced ~20x cost drops and single-digit-million annualized savings.

insights.claim: DoorDash built a single LLM Gateway offering one API and SDK across OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and open-source models, so teams can swap models by changing one config as new models appear every couple of months.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: Model-agnostic gateways commoditize model vendors and keep pricing power with the enterprise buyer.

insights.claim: Rate limits and quota shortages forced fallback routing, such as OpenAI with an Azure fallback or Claude API with a Bedrock fallback, to make production services reliable.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: Frontier-model capacity constraints are a real enterprise pain; cloud resellers act as redundancy and capture demand.

insights.claim: As usage grew, finance demanded cost attribution, so the gateway added workspaces to track and charge spend back to departments; the gateway also logs every request and response.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: LLM spend governance becomes a platform requirement at scale; tooling for per-team cost attribution is a product category.

insights.claim: Because the gateway was built company-wide, DoorDash easily onboarded acquired companies Wolt, Deliveroo and SevenRooms onto the same platform.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: Shared AI infrastructure creates integration synergy for acquisitions.

insights.claim: The gateway is the central place for before-hooks such as PII redaction and after-hooks that stop the model disparaging customers or recommending competitors; guardrails are opt-in, not enforced, and hallucination is handled via evals.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Enterprise guardrails remain voluntary even at a sophisticated adopter, suggesting governance is immature.

insights.claim: DoorDash went vendor-first because the field moves fast, but softened it after an evals vendor failed on custom tracing and annotation needs; the new rule is to own the workflow surface and buy or build the implementation.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Vendor-built eval/observability products lose when enterprises need custom workflows, a risk for point-solution startups.
insights.quote: In the end, we had to soften our stance on vendor first, and then we realized like, we need to own the workflow surface.
insights.locator: Chapter 3 - Vendor-First Taught us What to Own

insights.claim: Model deprecation cycles, such as Gemini's one-year model lifetime, force platform teams to migrate hundreds of use cases without a business justification.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Forced migrations push enterprises toward open weights and portability layers, a hidden cost of proprietary APIs.

insights.claim: At DoorDash's scale, quota constraints from proprietary providers and a steeply rising cost curve made portability a must-have rather than a nice-to-have.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Large-scale enterprise demand is outrunning frontier-lab capacity and pricing, which supports inference-compute demand and open-model adoption.

insights.claim: Teams switching from frontier proprietary models to open-weights models like Qwen3 and Qwen3 Embeddings saw accuracy increases and costs drop roughly 20x on a handful of use cases, yielding single-digit million-dollar annualized savings.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence of open-weights models displacing frontier APIs on cost at a large consumer-tech company.
insights.quote: They're actually seeing accuracy increase, and cost drops like 20x.

insights.claim: Open-weights models such as Qwen, GLM, Kimi and DeepSeek are good enough out of the box that adoption went through the roof once DoorDash had the self-hosting foundation, which the speaker did not expect a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Chinese open-weights models are gaining real enterprise share in US companies, pressuring frontier-lab pricing.

insights.claim: DoorDash serves its own models through the LLM Gateway on Modal, a Python-first GPU cloud, using vLLM and SGLang for serving and Hugging Face TRL, Unsloth or Axolotl for fine-tuning.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: Shows the open inference and fine-tuning stack and neoclouds, like Modal, that enterprises are choosing.

insights.claim: Teams should start on frontier proprietary models, which remain best on accuracy, and move to open weights, distillation or smaller models only when latency or cost becomes the constraint after product-market fit.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Frontier models keep the accuracy premium while cost-optimizing workloads migrate down-stack.

insights.claim: In 2025 DoorDash had 25-plus agent projects and agents on every laptop (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), and MCP's arrival was the critical moment that drew teams into building agents.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: MCP is a de facto standard shaping enterprise agent building.
insights.locator: Chapter 5 - Agents Changed the Primitive Again

insights.claim: DoorDash evolved from an MCP gateway into an agent gateway, handling authorization policies, tool-level access, rate limits, observability and a self-serve registry for more than 50 MCP servers, reaching 300,000 daily tool calls.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: Agent traffic is already hundreds of thousands of calls a day at one company, so agent identity and governance infrastructure is a growing market.

insights.claim: Agent identity and tool access became a major problem: an agent on a laptop can have broad permissions, but internal service agents must not inherit everything a human grants Claude Code, so MCP servers declare authorization policies and users choose which agents get which tools.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: Agent identity and authorization is an under-served security category to watch.

insights.claim: DoorDash designs for three audiences: human users, agents acting on behalf of humans, and agents as services.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Machine-identity management will have to cover agents as first-class principals.

insights.claim: The gateway is stateless for agent sessions and runtime orchestration, such as long-running agents and reconnecting after a pod dies, remains unsolved and left to product teams.
insights.speaker: Siddharth Kodwani
insights.so_what: Stateful, durable agent runtime is an open infrastructure gap.

insights.claim: DoorDash's GenAI platform has over 5,000 internal users with 45 onboarding daily, and about 40% are non-engineers in legal, sales, operations and strategy who use the APIs.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Non-engineer use broadens the enterprise AI user base well beyond developers, supporting seat- and usage-based demand.
insights.quote: Surprisingly, something I did not predict was that 40% of people are non-engineers.

insights.claim: The team's value proposition is helping product teams optimize accuracy, latency and cost; use cases cluster as automation reducing costs and recommendations/personalization raising revenue.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Reveals how a large marketplace frames GenAI ROI: cost-out automation and top-line personalization.

insights.claim: DoorDash chose APIs and SDKs over notebooks and GPU access because its customers shifted from ML engineers to all engineers.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: API-first consumption of AI is the pattern for broad enterprise adoption.

insights.claim: A signing of the first OpenAI contract in April 2023 felt like a very large spend, which in hindsight seems minor.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Illustrates how fast enterprise LLM spending scaled from tentative contracts.

insights.claim: Evals remain unsolved: DoorDash starts teams with tracing (OTel, Google ADK templates), then product metrics, evaluators (code or LLM-as-judge), custom dashboards and human annotation UIs, still with handholding.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Evals and tracing tooling is still immature, an opening for tooling vendors but a risk of in-house builds.

insights.claim: An agent skills marketplace lets staff install plugins so Claude Code, Codex or Cursor know DoorDash internal systems out of the box, and the team relies on this more than documentation to onboard non-engineers.
insights.speaker: Swaroop Chitlur
insights.so_what: Skills and plugins are becoming the distribution channel for enterprise agent capability.
